chapters.title: Chapter 6: Reporting and Getting It Right

lessons.title: Reporting Capital Gains in Your ITR: Broker P&L, CAS and Schedule CG

body.text: Filing is where a year of buying and selling becomes one number. The department already receives most of that data from your broker, fund house and registrar, so your job is to report it in the right schedule and make the two versions agree.

children.text: Nikhil, a 35-year-old hotel manager in Jaipur, had his first busy investing year: equity trades through a broker, mutual fund redemptions, a gold ETF sale and an inherited plot he finally sold. He had always filed a one-page return in fifteen minutes. This year that form was not even available to him.

body.caption: Which return form an investor needs

cells: ITR-1
Salary or pension, one or two house properties, other income, and long-term equity gains within the ₹1.25 lakh exemption
You have any other capital gains, any capital loss to carry forward, foreign assets or crypto
ITR-2
Any capital gains from shares, funds, property, gold, foreign assets or crypto, with no business income
You have business or professional income, including futures and options trading
ITR-3
Capital gains plus business or professional income, including intraday and F&O trading
Not applicable; this is the widest form for individuals

body.title: Nikhil's Form
body.question: Nikhil has salary, long-term equity gains of ₹3,20,000, a gold ETF sale, a plot sale and a short-term capital loss he wants to carry forward. He does no intraday or F&O trading. Which form does he file?
body.explanation: ITR-1 is out on three counts: gains above the ₹1.25 lakh exemption, gains from assets other than listed equity, and a loss to carry forward. He has no business income, so ITR-2 is the right form. Adding F&O or intraday trading would push him to ITR-3.

children.text: Step 2: Gather Four Sets of Records

cells: Tax P&L or capital gains report
Zerodha Console, Groww, Upstox and other brokers
Trade-wise and summary short-term and long-term gains, charges and STT, plus a ready file for scrip-wise reporting
Capital gains statement
MF Central, CAMS or KFintech
Lot-wise redemptions with FIFO applied, split into short-term and long-term
Annual Information Statement (AIS) and Form 26AS
Income tax e-filing portal
What brokers, registrars, banks and buyers have reported against your PAN, including TDS credits
Deal documents
Your own records
Sale deed, purchase deed, stamp duty and registration receipts, improvement bills, Form 26QB for property TDS, and Form 16 for any ESOP perquisite

body.text: Start from your own records, then reconcile with AIS. Doing it the other way round tempts you to accept whatever the AIS says, and AIS entries can be wrong: a corporate action can look like a sale, an off-market transfer can appear twice, and a joint holding can show in full against one PAN.

children.text: Step 3: Fill the Capital Gains Schedules

markDefs.definition: The capital gains schedule of the income tax return, split into a short-term section and a long-term section, with separate rows for each type of asset and rate.

children.text: In ITR-2 and ITR-3, capital gains go into
, which is split into a short-term part and a long-term part, with separate rows by asset and rate. Around it sit several supporting schedules.

body.caption: The schedules an investor usually touches

cells: Schedule CG
All capital gains and losses, by asset type and rate
Schedule 112A
Scrip-wise details of long-term equity gains: ISIN, name, units, sale value, cost and the 31 January 2018 fair market value for grandfathered holdings
Schedule CFL
Losses carried forward from earlier years and losses being carried forward from this year
Schedule SI
Income taxed at special rates, such as 20% short-term and 12.5% long-term gains
Schedule VDA
Every crypto transfer, trade by trade
Schedule FA
Foreign assets held during the calendar year, including US shares and RSUs

body.title: The Scrip-Wise Schedule
body.textWithBlank: Long-term equity gains where grandfathering applies are reported scrip by scrip in Schedule ___, with the ISIN and the 31 January 2018 fair market value.
body.explanation: Most brokers generate a ready-to-upload file for this schedule from your tax P&L, and MF Central does the same for mutual fund units, so you rarely have to type it in row by row.

events.title: Download the year's statements
events.description: Broker tax P&L, mutual fund capital gains statement, interest certificates and any property documents for the tax year just ended.

events.title: Check AIS and Form 26AS
events.description: Compare every reported sale and TDS entry with your own records and submit feedback in the AIS for anything wrong or duplicated.

events.title: Pay self-assessment tax
events.description: Compute the tax on your gains, subtract TDS and advance tax already paid, and pay the balance with any interest.

events.title: File the return
events.description: Usually 31 July for individuals who do not need an audit, though CBDT sometimes extends it. Filing by this date protects your right to carry losses forward.

events.title: E-verify
events.description: An unverified return is treated as not filed at all, which can cost you the carry forward as well.

body.title: Nikhil's Balance to Pay
body.prompt: Nikhil's total tax for the year works out to ₹96,000. TDS of ₹18,000 appears in his Form 26AS, and he has already paid ₹55,000 of advance tax. Ignoring interest, how much self-assessment tax must he pay before filing, in rupees?
body.explanation: ₹96,000 − ₹18,000 − ₹55,000 = ₹23,000. He pays this as self-assessment tax and enters the challan details in the return. Interest for late or short payment of advance tax is covered in the next lesson.

body.title: The AIS Says He Sold More Than He Did
body.scenario: Nikhil's AIS shows equity sales of ₹14,80,000, but his broker tax P&L shows ₹11,30,000. Digging in, he finds two causes: shares he transferred from an old demat account to his current one appear as a sale, and a joint holding with his brother is reported in full against his PAN.
body.prompt: What should he do, and what should he not do?
body.modelAnswer: He should report his real gains, computed from his own records, not the AIS figure. For each wrong entry he submits feedback in the AIS: the demat transfer is marked as information that is not a sale, and the joint holding is marked as relating to another person, with his brother reporting his share in his own return. He keeps the broker tax P&L, the demat transfer statement and evidence of the joint holding in case the department asks later. What he should not do is inflate his reported sale value to match the AIS, or ignore the mismatch and hope nobody notices, since unexplained gaps between AIS and the return are a common trigger for notices.

body.text: AIS is prefilled information, not an assessment. It can miss things too, particularly off-market deals, unlisted share sales and foreign transactions. You remain responsible for reporting income that is not in the AIS at all.

children.text: Property: the buyer deducts 1% TDS on purchases of ₹50 lakh or more and files Form 26QB. Check that the TDS reaches your Form 26AS with the correct PAN. The return asks for the buyer's details and the stamp duty value, so keep both ready.
Crypto: every transfer goes into Schedule VDA with dates, cost and sale value. Exchange-deducted TDS appears in the AIS and is claimed as a credit.
Foreign shares and RSUs: gains go into Schedule CG, the holdings go into Schedule FA for the calendar year, and any foreign tax credit needs the foreign tax credit form filed before the return.
ESOPs: the perquisite already sits in your Form 16 as salary. Only the later sale of the shares goes into Schedule CG, using the exercise-date value as cost.
Older returns: if you discover a mistake after filing, a revised return is possible within the allowed window, and an updated return can be filed later, though with additional tax.

body.label: Income Tax e-Filing Portal
body.description: Download your AIS, Form 26AS and prefilled return data, pay self-assessment tax, file the return and e-verify, all from the same login.

cards.definition: The capital gains schedule, split into short-term and long-term sections by asset and rate.
Scrip-wise reporting of long-term equity gains, with ISIN and 31 January 2018 fair market value.
Where brought-forward and carried-forward losses are reported.
Annual Information Statement: what third parties reported against your PAN. Prefilled information, not an assessment.
The balance tax you pay before filing, after TDS and advance tax credits.
Confirming the filed return within 30 days, without which it is treated as never filed.

body.title: Your Filing Checklist
steps: Download broker tax P&L and mutual fund capital gains statements for the full tax year
Pull AIS and Form 26AS and reconcile every sale and TDS entry against your records
Submit AIS feedback for duplicates, transfers wrongly shown as sales and joint holdings
Enter gains in Schedule CG, upload the scrip-wise file for Schedule 112A, and complete Schedule CFL for losses
Add Schedule VDA for crypto and Schedule FA for foreign holdings if they apply
Pay self-assessment tax, file by the due date and e-verify within 30 days

points: ITR-1 works only for small long-term equity gains within the exemption and no losses to carry forward
Most investors file ITR-2, and anyone trading F&O or intraday files ITR-3
Broker tax P&L and MF Central statements are your primary records; AIS is for reconciliation
Schedule CG holds the gains, with Schedule 112A, CFL, SI, VDA and FA supporting it
Fix AIS mismatches through feedback rather than changing your figures to match
File by the due date and e-verify within 30 days, or you lose the carry forward of losses

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and is not tax or investment advice. Form names, schedule names and due dates reflect the position at the time of writing; CBDT notifies new return forms each year, and the first returns under the Income-tax Act, 2025 for tax year 2026-27 are filed in 2027, so confirm the current forms and dates on the e-filing portal. Consult a qualified tax professional before filing.
